answer: A graph-based trust protocol limits Sybil attacks by scoring identities via random walks from trusted seed nodes. An attacker incurs the scarce cost of establishing legitimate inbound attestations from reputable peers, as closed collusive loops cannot span topological bottlenecks. Whether an autonomous probe relays a telemetry signal across a canyon or inspects a quarry ledge, fake clusters remain discounted. However, this mechanism penalizes honest newcomers with severe cold-start friction.
